source.title: Choosing the right basis for interpretability: Psychophysical comparison between neuron-based and dictionary-based representations
source.authors: Julien Colin; L. Goetschalckx; Thomas Fel; Victor Boutin; Thomas Serre; Nuria Oliver

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports evidence that neuron-based representations can be less visually coherent to human observers than dictionary-based representations, and argues that neuron-only model comparisons can mislead. It does not directly measure the claim versions’ specified neuron shares, language models, activation-prediction failures, or automated explanation scores.
record.gate_note: The study measures human success at identifying a visual pattern from reference images and query images in ResNet50 and VGG16. This is related to neuron interpretability, but it does not report the proportion of neurons with one or more jobs, test Qwen3 or language models, or measure whether explanations predict actual neuron activations. Prior-work results mentioned in the paper are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: Human psychophysics on ResNet50 and VGG16 compares how visually coherent neuron-based and dictionary-based (NMF/CRAFT) units are. It reports no share of single-job neurons, no language models, no InceptionV1 cat/car analysis, no attribution graphs and no simulation scoring. The 2AFC task contrasts maximally with minimally activating images, so it cannot show an activating-example explanation failing to predict firing (V6). The superposition framing bears on the essay's thesis but on no stated version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that ResNet50 shows more superposition than VGG16. ResNet50 appears more interpretable only under the dictionary basis, so neuron-only model comparisons can mislead and prior results may need reinterpreting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CRAFT with non-negative matrix factorization and human psychophysics in computer-vision CNNs; it does not use the Qwen3 pole audit or the cited language-model explanation-scoring procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The dictionary-versus-neuron advantage was reported in all three experiments. The dictionary-based condition showed a positive depth correlation in both models; the neuron-based correlations were not significant after correction.

fits_no_version.finding: Humans identify the shared pattern of dictionary elements more accurately than that of neurons: 83.5 vs 78.8, 85.1 vs 76.2 (ResNet50) and 81.5 vs 77.1 (VGG16).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ImageNet CNNs, NMF dictionary elements are more visually coherent to humans than individual neurons, with the gap growing in deeper layers.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet50 dictionary elements are less axis-aligned than VGG16's (0.40 vs 0.45). ResNet50 is more interpretable under the dictionary basis (85.1 vs 81.5, p = 0.016) but not under the neuron basis (z = 0.56, p = 0.71).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model comparisons of interpretability depend on whether units are neurons or dictionary elements; neuron-only comparisons can mask differences linked to superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Dictionary elements are as important as, or slightly more important than, matched neurons under Gradient×Input.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The NMF elements compared here are at least as decision-relevant as the neurons they are matched to.

record.problems: Only two vision models were tested. The paper says the semantic-confound control was only partially successful; its task measures human visual-pattern identification rather than actual activation prediction. The paper also says future work should test dictionary learning on full layer activations.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported study results meeting the row criteria were left out. Results cited from prior work were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B pole audit or job-count shares.
No language models, dense or MoE, and no scale analysis.
No InceptionV1 cat/car neuron analysis and no test of recursive generalization.

No share of interpretable neurons, no InceptionV1-sized estimates, and no manipulation of architecture, regularization or tools. ResNet50 vs VGG16 is compared only on dictionary axis-alignment and human coherence.
No attribution graphs and no replacement-model comparison.
The query task contrasts top versus bottom activating images. It does not test whether an explanation predicts where a neuron fires across its activation range.
No automated simulation scoring of explanations.

missing.what: Cross-model comparison. Dictionary basis: ResNet50 85.1 vs VGG16 81.5 (z = 2.14, p = 0.016). Neuron basis: no difference (z = 0.56, p = 0.71).

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'discusses/T5' is overstated: the paper never engages the essay or its versions. T6 with fits_no_version is more accurate. Its results lean toward the superposition view the essay disputes, but no version is stated in neuron-vs-dictionary terms. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B or report the share of neuron poles with one job, two jobs, or unknown jobs.
Uses two convolutional vision models, not other language models; does not compare dense and mixture-of-experts language models or scale to trillions of parameters.
Does not test the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or whether it detects pose through recursive generalization.

Compares neuron and dictionary bases in ResNet50 and VGG16, but does not measure the share of interpretable neurons, test the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates, or establish that architecture, regularization, and tool quality cause the stated change.
Does not build attribution graphs or test whether model behavior can be explained without a trained replacement model and reconstruction error.
The human task asks observers to identify a visual pattern in query images; it does not test whether an explanation predicts where a neuron actually fires on new inputs.
Does not score automated neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Human visual-coherence task; compare dictionary-based and neuron-based representations.
rows.measure: Mean proportion of correct query-image selections (interpretability).
rows.uncertainty: The paper states the ± values correspond to 95% confidence intervals; Mann–Whitney U test z = 3.12, p < .001.
rows.note: The authors describe this as the same neuron-based protocol used in Zimmermann et al. (2023), with dictionary-based trials added.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Human visual-coherence task with semantic-confound control; compare dictionary-based and neuron-based representations.
rows.measure: Mean proportion of correct query-image selections (interpretability).
rows.uncertainty: The paper states the ± values correspond to 95% confidence intervals; Mann–Whitney U test z = 4.83, p < .001.
rows.note: One unit that could not be controlled for semantic labels was excluded from both basis conditions.

rows.uncertainty: The paper states the ± values correspond to 95% confidence intervals; Mann–Whitney U test z = 2.46, p = 0.01.

rows.check: State is acceptable only after Bonferroni correction. Uncorrected, p = 0.04 is nominally significant; the note should make this explicit.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Measure average axis-alignment of CRAFT dictionary elements using Hoyer sparsity.
rows.uncertainty: Mann–Whitney U test z = 6.01, p < .001; no error bar stated.
rows.note: Lower axis-alignment indicates dictionary elements are more distributed across neuron axes; the authors interpret this as consistent with greater superposition in ResNet50.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Measure average axis-alignment of CRAFT dictionary elements using Hoyer sparsity.
rows.uncertainty: Mann–Whitney U test z = 6.01, p < .001; no error bar stated.
rows.note: Higher axis-alignment indicates dictionary elements are closer to individual neuron axes.
rows.check: This duplicates R8 (same comparison, sides swapped). It should be merged with R8 rather than kept as a separate row.
